日本の担い手.quote: Honestly, we don't fully agree on it ourselves. One camp says it comes from the Japanese

In our view, the origin of the word “Azumuta” has a double meaning. On the one hand, it comes from the Japanese word (始 め た) for “I have begun” and leads to various explanations such as an action, a new beginning, personal commitment, responsibility, self-assurance, and hope. On the other hand, it also comes from the Flemish expression “Azo moeta”, “zo moet dat “/ “aha, zo moet dat”.

And the name? It comes from the Japanese “始めた”, which translates to “I have started”, though locals in Ghent will tell you it also sounds a lot like “*ah zo moet da*”, dialect for “that’s how it’s done”.
